steps: Define collection objective and legal/organizational authorization
Preserve source timestamps and original artifact metadata
Record acquisition utility, version, operator and time
Hash and store securely with access log and chain of custody
Analyze copies and note completeness/limitations

runbooks.title: Detection deployment
steps: Document data contract and normalization fields
Write behavioral detection with owner, runbook and ATT&CK mapping
Construct positive and negative test fixtures
Test performance, tuning and missing data behavior
Deploy via change control; monitor and maintain version history

runbooks.title: Validate endpoint process alert
steps: Confirm asset identity, criticality and EDR telemetry freshness
Record process GUID, image path, command line, parent and signer
Verify alert action: blocked, alert-only, quarantined or failed
Look for child processes, file writes, network destinations and persistence
Check user context, change schedule and peer hosts
Document confirmed behaviors, uncertainty and escalation owner

runbooks.title: Investigate Windows failed logons
steps: Establish affected accounts, endpoints, sources and UTC timeframe
Review 4625 status/substatus and logon type where available
Group by source and distinct users; check success-after-failure
Check VPN/SSO/IdP context and source reputation
Inspect successful-session behavior before declaring takeover
Escalate credential abuse with account owner and scope

runbooks.title: Investigate new local administrator
steps: Confirm group scope and member/actor from Security audit
Correlate user/device sign-in, ticket and maintenance records
Determine privilege granted and persistence possibilities
Pivot on actor changes to other assets
Escalate unauthorized access under approved identity process
Preserve relevant account and group audit records

runbooks.title: Inspect mail authentication headers
steps: Preserve full message and Message-ID
Read Received chain and authenticated sender domain
Compare From, Reply-To, envelope and DMARC alignment
Examine URL/attachment without unsafe execution
Correlate recipients, clicks and endpoint effects
Document campaign scope and recommended user notification

runbooks.title: Investigate WAF suspicious request
steps: Record client, rule, action, request ID and UTC time
Decode only within approved tooling; preserve raw URI
Compare WAF decision to application and upstream logs
Look for successful adjacent requests and error patterns
Consider false positives and known scanners/change windows
Escalate supported exploitation evidence, not only a suspicious payload

runbooks.title: Recover missing SIEM log source
steps: Check collector status, heartbeat and data freshness
Compare raw source generation with index/search volume
Identify TLS, auth, storage, parser or pipeline issues
Notify coverage owner and affected on-call analysts
Record visibility gap period and affected detections
Replay test event and confirm ingestion after repair

runbooks.title: Investigate unusual outbound DNS
steps: Confirm device, user and resolver source
Group qname/qtype/rcode, timing and subdomain diversity
Check proxy/network destinations after DNS answers
Identify owning process in EDR/Sysmon where possible
Compare with corporate update/sync tools
Escalate suspicious correlated behavior with gap notes

runbooks.title: Investigate suspect remote service execution
steps: Collect 4624 type 3, 4648 and service event 7045 where enabled
Join by account/source/target and narrow UTC windows
Inspect ImagePath, new service binary, hash and signer
Check target processes and outbound connections
Search same actor/service name across estate
Coordinate evidence and approved containment if malicious

runbooks.title: Investigate Kerberos abuse
steps: Validate domain controller security audit coverage
Baseline 4768/4769 volume by source and SPN
Identify highly privileged service accounts and legacy encryption
Correlate suspicious source workstation and authentication chain
Investigate post-auth privileges and lateral movement
Recommend credential response through domain owner

runbooks.title: Investigate OAuth application consent
steps: Identify actor/app ID, consent time, tenant and effective scopes
Verify publisher and authorization/request history
Review interactive and noninteractive sign-ins and app API operations
Scope affected mailboxes/files and possible persistent credentials
Coordinate removal/revocation with cloud tenant owner
Document access limits, gaps and remaining token risk

runbooks.title: Investigate cloud object access
steps: Confirm bucket/container policy and principal identity
Review management changes and data read events where available
Calculate exposure window and list accessed sensitive objects
Check approved workflows, access key history and source network
Coordinate permission rollback and credential response
Engage data owner, legal and notification process where applicable

runbooks.title: Triage Linux SSH and persistence
steps: Validate sshd logins by account, IP and time
Review sudo/auditd commands and shell history cautiously
Inspect systemd services, timers, cron and authorized_keys
Find binary location, ownership, hash and network connections
Check service account/change approvals
Preserve evidence and escalate with Linux owner

runbooks.title: Contain identity takeover
steps: Verify current compromise indicators and incident authority
Identify accounts, sessions, grants, keys and privileged operations
Assess business impact of disablement, revocation and rotation
Execute coordinated approved containment steps
Validate reauthentication/token invalidation and persistence removal
Monitor for reentry and record recovery verification

runbooks.title: Ransomware crisis first 15 minutes
steps: Identify confirmed encryption, notes and affected shares
Page incident command and infrastructure owners per policy
Coordinate urgent authorized isolation and privileged identity controls
Preserve available volatile and disk evidence without delaying response
Validate backup isolation and core business impact
Track each action, owner, timestamp and restoration plan

runbooks.title: Validate detection through purple team
steps: Write technique hypothesis and safe test boundaries
Confirm required source coverage and parser fields
Generate a synthetic or lab-approved known-positive trace
Verify ingestion and alert correctness on monitored hosts
Test realistic negatives and measure false-positive cost
File coverage, logic and response improvements with owners

runbooks.title: Build threat-hunt notebook
steps: Record hypothesis, asset cohort and threat rationale
Enumerate necessary telemetry and known blind spots
Save exact queries, timestamps and normalized results
Document leads and tests that disconfirm hypothesis
Escalate discovered incidents through normal case system
Deliver new detection candidates and visibility recommendations

runbooks.title: Perform detection rule post-deployment QA
steps: Verify parser/source health and expected field types
Run positive fixtures and representative benign events
Measure latency, rule execution cost and alert volumes
Review exceptions and tune only with documented justification
Compare outcomes to versioned baseline and rollout objectives
Keep rollback plan, owner, and measured follow-up date

runbooks.title: Run post-incident improvement review
steps: Collect verified incident timeline and business effects
Identify root and compounding factors including detection delays
Document successful controls and data gaps
Assign measurable fixes, owners and deadlines
Validate high-priority fixes with tabletop or technical tests
Track completion and communicate residual risks

glossary.definition: A notification that a detection rule or security sensor observed suspicious or notable behavior.
An event or series of events that actually or potentially jeopardizes security and needs coordinated handling.
A recorded observation from a system or service.
Logic that marks events or patterns as important.
Rapid evidence-led validation, contextualization and prioritization of alerts.
Handing off a case with sufficient evidence and urgency to the appropriate owner.
Recorded conclusion about alert outcome, such as true, false or benign positive.
Assessment of potential or actual technical and business impact.
Operational urgency after considering impact, activity, SLA and other work.
How strongly available evidence supports an assessment.
Service Level Agreement; a defined service obligation including response or resolution time.
Mean Time To Detect, requiring an explicit definition of incident start and detection time.
Mean Time To Respond or Resolve depending on team definition; define it before comparing.
A detector fired incorrectly relative to its stated matching intent.
A correct suspicious-pattern match with a legitimate explanation.
Indicator of compromise: observable such as suspicious hash, URL, domain or IP.
Tactics, Techniques and Procedures: how an adversary operates.
An adversary objective such as credential access or lateral movement.
A documented way adversaries achieve a tactic.
Linking separate events by meaningful keys and time.
Adding context such as asset ownership, identity privilege and intelligence.
Recorded data about behavior, activity and health of systems.
Transferring source records into an analytics system.
Mapping multiple data formats to a usable common structure.
Extracting fields from original log text or structured records.
How long records are stored and available for investigation.
Security Information and Event Management for logging, correlation, detection and search.
Security Orchestration, Automation and Response workflows and integrations.
Endpoint Detection and Response: endpoint telemetry, detection and investigation/response.
Extended Detection and Response: correlated detection and response across multiple sources.
Network Detection and Response based on network telemetry and analytics.
Intrusion Detection System; produces alerts for suspicious activity.
Intrusion Prevention System; can prevent or block matching activity.
Web Application Firewall: inspects and acts on web request patterns.
Network or host control enforcing allowed and denied communications.
Intermediary handling requests, potentially logging web context.
Network Address Translation; rewrites IP and/or port at boundary.
Classless Inter-Domain Routing; compact representation of IP networks.
Reliable ordered transport protocol based on a connection and sequence acknowledgements.
Datagram transport without built-in delivery or ordering assurances.
TCP flag used to begin connection establishment.
TCP flag for resetting a connection.
Domain Name System: distributed service for resolving domain-related records.
Time To Live; DNS cache lifetime or IP hop limit depending on context.
DNS record mapping a hostname to an IPv4 address.
DNS record mapping a hostname to an IPv6 address.
DNS canonical name alias record.
DNS record routing mail for a domain.
DNS text record used for many purposes including mail authentication.
DNS response indicating the queried name does not exist.
Hypertext Transfer Protocol used for web requests and responses.
HTTP protected with TLS, typically on port 443.
Transport Layer Security, providing authenticated encrypted transport.
Server Name Indication in TLS for communicating intended hostname in applicable handshakes.
A network fingerprinting technique derived from client TLS/HTTP characteristics; not a verdict.
Digital credential binding public key information to a subject under a trust model.
Sender Policy Framework; domain authorizes sending IPs.
DomainKeys Identified Mail; verifies digital signatures on mail.
Mail policy/alignment mechanism built on SPF and/or DKIM.
Business Email Compromise, social engineering targeting financial/business transactions.
Deceptive message trying to induce harmful action or disclose information.
Multi-Factor Authentication using distinct categories of verification factors.
Repeated push prompts intended to trick or pressure a user into approval.
Single Sign-On: access multiple services through one identity flow.
Framework for delegated authorization; grants and tokens require careful scoping.
Credential-like data representing a session or delegated authorization.
Policies evaluating authentication and device/context to permit or restrict access.
Identity and Access Management for authentication, roles and access policy.
Microsoft directory service for identities and domain policy.
Server providing Active Directory domain services and authentication.
Directory access protocol used by systems including Active Directory.
Ticket-based network authentication protocol.
Kerberos Ticket Granting Ticket used to request service tickets.
Ticket Granting Service; provides service tickets in Kerberos.
Microsoft authentication protocol family still present in some environments.
Service Principal Name associated with a Kerberos service identity.
Attempts one or few passwords against many accounts.
Repeated guessing of credentials, commonly concentrated on an account or secret.
Using previously exposed username/password pairs on other services.
Authentication technique abusing NTLM hash material instead of a plaintext password.
Windows process responsible for security policy and authentication-related secrets.
System Monitor; configurable Windows event telemetry tool from Microsoft Sysinternals.
Windows successful logon audit event.
Windows failed logon audit event.
Windows process creation audit event when configured.
Windows System event commonly indicating new service installation.
Windows Security audit log was cleared.
PowerShell script block logging event when configured.
Process creation event when collected.
Network connection event when collected.
DNS query event when collected.
Parent-child relationships between processes.
Legitimate operating system binaries that can be abused by attackers.
Technique for maintaining access across time, logouts or reboots.
Obtaining a higher level of permissions.
Moving from one system or security context to another.
Communication channel used to direct compromised systems.
Repeated client communication that may indicate scheduled C2 activity.
Unauthorized transfer of data out of a security boundary.
Malware or intrusion activity that encrypts/denies access and demands payment.
Splunk Search Processing Language for data exploration and analysis.
Kusto Query Language used in platforms such as Microsoft Sentinel.
Generic YAML-based SIEM detection rule format with translation pipelines.
Rule language for classifying file or memory patterns, subject to configuration.
Expected behavior established from comparable historic observations.
Testable statement predicting observable adversary behavior.
Designing, implementing, testing and maintaining reliable detections.
Version-controlled, tested and deployable detection content.
Among positive detector results, fraction that are true positives.
Among actual malicious positives, fraction the detector identified.
Documented evidence acquisition, storage, access and transfers.
Preserved copy of digital media or memory made with documented method.
Action to limit an incident's current or future spread/impact.
Removing malicious access, persistence and cause after containment.
Restoring services and verifying they remain secure.
Structured learning process examining sequence, impacts and control improvements.
Identifying possible adversary actions and controls within a system design.
Threat-modeling categories: spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, elevation of privilege.
High-level representation of stages in an attack or intrusion.
AWS API audit logging service; supported event categories require configuration.
Role-Based Access Control for Kubernetes API permissions.
Non-human identity used by a workload or automated service.
Packaged filesystem/config used to instantiate container processes.
Advanced Security Information Model: Microsoft normalization approach for Sentinel telemetry across products.
Elastic Common Schema: a field-name framework for normalizing log and security event data.
Splunk metadata that helps determine how incoming events are interpreted and searched.
Timestamp claimed by the event source, potentially subject to clock drift or parser error.
Timestamp when a logging pipeline receives an event; often later than event generation.
Windows remote interactive logon type often associated with RDP.
Windows network logon type; common for SMB and other remote resource access.
Windows Security event for new process creation when auditing is enabled.
Windows System event indicating installation of a service.
Windows DC Security event concerning a Kerberos service-ticket request.
Windows Security object-operation event; its interpretation for directory access requires SACL and object context.
Windows Security event for user-account creation.
Windows Security event for adding a member to a security-enabled local group.
Identifier used by Sysmon to correlate a process across events more reliably than PID alone.
Sysmon file-create event when configured.
Attack pattern involving requests for service tickets that could be attacked offline if weak credentials are used.
Abuse of directory replication rights to retrieve password data from Active Directory.
Authorization granting an application specific delegated or application permissions to access resources.
Credential artifact used to obtain new access tokens, depending on identity provider and policy.
Tenant identity representing an application or service that can be assigned permissions.
Behavior such as backup tampering that may precede encryption but does not itself prove active encryption.
Audit record for resource configuration or management operation.
Audit record for resource-level object or data access where logging is enabled.
Access control list applied to a stored object or container, depending on provider configuration.
Small controlled rollout used to monitor a change before broad production deployment.
An attack or defined positive behavior that the relevant detection fails to alert on.
Missing or delayed observations that reduce confidence in investigation or detection coverage.
Coordinated attacker-behavior simulation and defense validation exercise.
Kubernetes volume configuration that mounts part of the underlying node filesystem.
Role-based access control, granting permissions based on assigned roles.
API-server records describing requests, actors, resources and outcomes based on configured audit policy.
Kubernetes identity that processes in pods may use for API access.
Windows artifact storing application/file metadata with forensic interpretation limitations.
Windows application compatibility artifact that cannot alone prove exact execution events.
Windows artifact that can help infer application execution subject to OS and policy limitations.
Exploit Prediction Scoring System, providing an estimate of probability that a CVE will be exploited in the wild.
Matching domain relationships required by DMARC between visible From and authenticated identifiers.
Time-bounded assignment of IP address to network client, useful for historical device attribution.
Mail action automatically redirecting messages; malicious creation can indicate account compromise.
Controls and telemetry for detecting/restricting sensitive content movement.
Organization-dependent high-priority incident category generally requiring urgent ownership and communication.
Processing backlog that slows log pipeline throughput and may delay detections.
Periodic sensor/connector signal used to validate that data collection is still operating.
Known expected-positive or expected-negative synthetic event used for analytics testing.

questions.question: A /24 IPv4 subnet normally contains how many address slots?
questions.why: It has 2^(32-24) = 256 total addresses; classic /24 gives 254 usable host addresses.

questions.question: Which range is private IPv4?
Which happens first during a TCP connection handshake?
questions.why: SYN begins a standard TCP three-way handshake.

questions.question: A firewall log shows HTTPS but not the URL path. Why?
questions.why: Without decryption or proxy access, the path is usually encrypted.

questions.question: What DNS response means a name does not exist?
questions.why: NXDOMAIN means the queried DNS name does not exist.

questions.question: What is the best interpretation of a valid TLS certificate?
options: Identity validation under a certificate chain, not safety
questions.why: Phishing websites can obtain certificates.

questions.question: Which is an authentication factor?
questions.why: A hardware authenticator can prove possession.

questions.question: What does least privilege reduce?
questions.why: It constrains authorized actions and blast radius.

questions.question: What is a hash useful for in incident response?
questions.why: Hash is content-derived and does not establish intent.

questions.question: A public IP shared by employees maps to a suspicious connection. What is missing?
questions.why: IP-only attribution is unreliable under shared egress.

questions.question: What is a log ingestion gap?
questions.why: Absence of records may indicate collection failure.

questions.question: Which is a tactic in MITRE ATT&CK?
questions.why: Tactics describe adversary objectives.

questions.question: An alert says PowerShell ran. Best next question?
options: What launched it and what did it do?
questions.why: Parent process, command line, network and follow-on activity supply context.

questions.question: Which event normally signifies successful Windows logon?
questions.why: Windows Security Event 4624 reports a successful logon.

questions.question: Which event normally reports failed logon?
questions.why: Windows Security Event 4625 records a failed logon.

questions.question: New Windows service installation commonly appears as?
questions.why: Event 7045 in System log reports installation of a service.

questions.question: Sysmon Event 1 commonly records?
questions.why: When configured, Sysmon Event ID 1 is process creation.

questions.question: Sysmon Event 3 commonly records?
questions.why: Event ID 3 is network connection when enabled.

questions.question: Sysmon Event 22 commonly records?
questions.why: Sysmon 22 records DNS query events when configured.

questions.question: Several users get one failed sign-in each from one IP. Best initial hypothesis?
questions.why: Few attempts across many accounts indicate spraying.

questions.question: What makes an impossible-travel alert less convincing?
questions.why: VPN egress often shifts apparent geographic origin.

questions.question: What does SPF validate?
options: Authorized sending infrastructure for envelope identity
questions.why: SPF covers source IP authorization for a sending domain.

questions.question: What does DKIM add?
questions.why: DKIM can validate integrity and claimed signing domain.

questions.question: DMARC fundamentally deals with?
options: Mail authentication alignment and domain policy
questions.why: DMARC aligns identifiers with SPF/DKIM and publishes policies.

questions.question: What should you do with a reported suspicious URL?
options: Open it on your work laptop
Assume it is harmless if HTTPS
questions.why: Use isolated or approved analysis and preserve evidence.

questions.question: An EDR alert indicates a script was blocked. What can you conclude?
options: Reported prevention occurred, verify follow-on activity
questions.why: A block does not prove no other stage succeeded.

questions.question: An approved scan triggered the scan detector. Most accurate?
questions.why: Detection matched the behavior; authorization changes impact assessment.

questions.question: What should be in a high-quality escalation?
options: Evidence, timeline, scope, confidence and next action
questions.why: The receiving analyst needs reproducible pivots.

questions.question: What does HTTP 403 alone show?
questions.why: 403 doesn't identify why unless correlated with application/WAF logs.

questions.question: Which is a safer interpretation of a WAF SQLi alert?
options: Request matched a suspicious pattern, verify backend impact
questions.why: Rule hit is not proof of successful exploit.

questions.question: What is the most valuable next pivot after a suspicious successful sign-in?
options: Subsequent sensitive actions and session context
questions.why: Activity after authentication can support or weaken compromise hypothesis.

questions.question: What does Splunk stats count by user do?
options: Groups records by user and counts each group
questions.why: stats aggregates event data.

questions.question: What does KQL summarize count() by Account do?
questions.why: summarize is aggregation.

questions.question: When do you mark a SIEM alert false positive?
options: When evidence indicates detection logic or data is inaccurate
Whenever a user says it is fine
Every time no IOC reputation hit
questions.why: Authorized activity matching correctly may be benign positive.

questions.question: What should an SOC shift start include?
options: Handover, urgent queues and telemetry health
questions.why: Security posture depends on both open incidents and visibility.

questions.question: Which statement best defines a hypothesis?
questions.why: Alternative explanations and tests distinguish disciplined investigation.

questions.question: Why normalize event times to UTC?
questions.why: Different local time zones otherwise distort timeline.

questions.question: What is NOT guaranteed by resetting a compromised password?
options: Revocation of all previously stolen tokens
questions.why: Persistent sessions and app grants may require separate actions.

questions.question: Which trio strongly suggests ransomware?
options: Mass renames, shadow deletion, ransom notes
One VPN failure, email open, DNS answer
Normal backups, Windows update, browser use
questions.why: Combined behaviors imply active encryption and recovery sabotage.

questions.question: What is the best lateral movement evidence?
options: Remote logon plus service/task execution on another host
Same user on two laptops legally
questions.why: Behavior across hosts and credentials matters.

questions.question: A proxy shows repeated 60s contacts to unknown domain. Next?
options: Correlate endpoint process, prevalence and bytes
questions.why: Beaconing is a hypothesis needing context.

questions.question: Most useful to assess possible cloud exfiltration?
options: Object-level access logs and data volume
questions.why: Management logging alone may not show object reads.

questions.question: What does containment aim to do?
options: Limit current or future spread and impact
questions.why: Eradication and recovery are distinct phases.

questions.question: What is chain of custody?
questions.why: Evidence handling includes who, when, where and integrity.

questions.question: What does precision measure?
questions.why: Precision measures correctness of positive detections.

questions.question: What does recall measure?
questions.why: Recall measures fraction of actual positives detected.

questions.question: What is a risky tuning strategy?
options: Ignore all events from a large IP range
questions.why: Broad exclusions cause avoidable detection blind spots.

questions.question: What is Sigma best described as?
options: Generic YAML detection specification needing mapping
questions.why: Backend and field translation need testing.

questions.question: What should a hypothesis-driven case note include?
questions.why: Avoid confirmation bias.

questions.question: Why might an incident require legal stakeholder coordination?
options: Data exposure, regulation and notification requirements vary
EDR requires a lawyer to search logs
questions.why: Legal/compliance obligations depend on organization and jurisdiction.

questions.question: What differentiates hunting from reactive triage?
options: Every hunt must start with IOC list
Hunting is always malware reverse engineering
questions.why: Threat hunting begins without a necessarily existing alert.

questions.question: When is a negative hunt result trustworthy?
options: Data coverage and search assumptions were verified
The query ran without syntax errors
The dashboard had no red alerts
questions.why: Visibility and test validity are essential.

questions.question: What proves ATT&CK detection coverage?
options: Tested telemetry and rules detect behavior in scope
questions.why: Empirical validation is necessary.

questions.question: What should detection-as-code include?
questions.why: Engineering manages lifecycle not just query writing.

questions.question: Which is a strong negative test for a service-creation rule?
questions.why: Check benign behavior doesn't incorrectly fire.

questions.question: A host has no EDR events for hours. Most justified statement?
options: The host is offline for sure
questions.why: Collection failure is not evidence of safety.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of a post-incident review?
options: Improve controls through verified contributing factors
questions.why: Focus on operational learning and measurable fixes.

questions.question: A container runs suspicious code. Which context is essential?
options: Pod, image digest, service account and Kubernetes audit
questions.why: Workload identity and orchestration context guide scope.

questions.question: A hash search yields no hits. What does that mean?
options: Exact hash not seen in available data; variants may exist
questions.why: Coverage and hash specificity limit conclusions.

questions.question: SOC closed 50% more alerts this month. Is security improved?
options: Not necessarily: evaluate quality, risk, coverage and impact
questions.why: Closure volume is an output, not an effectiveness measure.

questions.question: Which transport protocol establishes sessions using a three-way handshake?
questions.why: TCP normally uses SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK to establish a connection.

questions.question: What does a DNS CNAME record represent?
questions.why: CNAME aliases one DNS name to another name.

questions.question: What does an HTTP 302 usually indicate?
questions.why: A 302 points the client to a different URL; follow the chain for investigation.

questions.question: Which Windows logon type usually represents RDP?
questions.why: RemoteInteractive is typically logon type 10; type 3 indicates a network logon.

questions.question: Which event typically records Windows service installation in the System log?
questions.why: System Event 7045 is service installation; context is required to determine legitimacy.

questions.question: Which event commonly records a successful Windows logon?
questions.why: Security 4624 records a logon success when audited.

questions.question: Why is a SHA-256 hash useful in an investigation?
options: To identify and verify specific file bytes
To prove the file is malicious
questions.why: A digest is a content fingerprint; reputation and behavior still determine risk.

questions.question: What does SPF pass establish?
options: The sending IP is authorized for the tested envelope identity
The visible From display name is genuine
questions.why: SPF is a domain authentication input, not a verdict on intent.

questions.question: What is a weakness of IOC-only detection?
options: Indicators rotate and may miss behavior
An IOC always uniquely identifies an actor
IOCs cannot ever be used in SIEM
questions.why: Behavioral analytics and context improve resilience to indicator changes.

questions.question: Which source helps map an IP to a device at a historical timestamp?
questions.why: Historical leases and switch/NAC records support temporal attribution.

questions.question: What is the main difference between an event timestamp and ingestion timestamp?
options: Event time is when it occurred; ingestion time is when a collector received it
questions.why: Collector delay and time drift can affect timeline reconstruction.

questions.question: What does principle of least privilege mean?
options: Grant only access needed for a task
questions.why: Excessive permission increases blast radius.

questions.question: A WAF blocks a traversal request with HTTP 403. What is directly supported?
options: That request was blocked at the WAF
questions.why: The WAF action addresses this request; investigate other attempts separately.

questions.question: EDR says action=alert_only. What is a safe conclusion?
options: The system alerted; no block is demonstrated
questions.why: Alert-only is not prevention. Confirm execution and subsequent behavior.

questions.question: Windows event 4625 usually indicates what?
questions.why: 4625 is a failed logon event under appropriate auditing.

questions.question: Which signal most strongly raises password-spraying risk?
options: One source failing across many users then succeeding
questions.why: Cross-user failures from one origin with later success are a suspicious pattern.

questions.question: A file download gets HTTP 200 and EDR blocks execution. Which summary is accurate?
options: Download observed, execution prevented by EDR
questions.why: Do not equate successful HTTP download with successful binary execution.

questions.question: Which artifact most helps confirm process ancestry?
questions.why: Stable process GUID links support process-tree reconstruction.

questions.question: What belongs in an escalation handoff?
options: Timestamped evidence, affected entities, impact, unknowns and next steps
Only a screenshot of the red alert
questions.why: Reproducible evidence and specific action requests prevent lost context.

questions.question: A sign-in succeeded with MFA from a corporate VPN egress. What should be checked?
options: Device/session context and VPN egress mapping
questions.why: MFA and VPN can explain anomalies but do not exclude compromise.

questions.question: What should happen when EDR connector lag exceeds a shift?
options: Raise visibility/ingestion issue and qualify conclusions
questions.why: Loss of visibility means zero alert count is not safety evidence.

questions.question: What best distinguishes a benign positive from a false positive?
options: Behavior matched the detection but was authorized
Both mean rule engine was broken
questions.why: Benign positive is correctly detected activity lacking malicious intent.

questions.question: What is the best first pivot for a phishing link click?
options: Check proxy download and endpoint execution with user/time
Send link to teammates to click
questions.why: Separate message receipt, click, download and execution.

questions.question: Which query flaw can cause silent data loss?
options: Assuming all sources use the same field name
questions.why: Schema normalization must be validated across sourcetypes.

questions.question: A 7045 follows remote type-3 logons from new source. What is the priority pivot?
options: Service image, creator, source account and business change
Conclude no lateral movement is possible
questions.why: Multiple corroborating events establish a plausible execution chain.

questions.question: A cloud trail has ListBuckets and GetObject. What do they prove respectively?
options: Enumeration and API object retrieval events
questions.why: API events require response, principal and downstream context for impact assessment.

questions.question: Which control reduces risk after OAuth app grant abuse?
options: Review and revoke grant/session under approved response
questions.why: Credential rotation alone may not remove malicious app permissions.

questions.question: Which statement about Kerberoasting is most accurate?
options: Unusual service ticket requests can be a clue, not proof of cracked credentials
questions.why: Interpret 4769 with source, SPN, account baseline and later behavior.

questions.question: Which approach best handles ransomware-like mass renaming?
options: Coordinate urgent containment, preserve evidence, scope impact
Wait a week for signature updates
Assume it is authorized change regardless of context
questions.why: Impact telemetry and backup tampering elevate urgency.

questions.question: What must an incident timeline state?
options: Event time, source, timezone and uncertainty
questions.why: Timestamps must be normalized and source delays/clock drift noted.

questions.question: What does a signed binary guarantee?
options: Only that signature verification ties to a key and signed bytes
That it has no network access
questions.why: A legitimate key may sign an abused or compromised program.

questions.question: Which is a risky rule-tuning approach?
options: Permanently excluding a broad subnet without tests
Testing expected positive and negative samples
questions.why: Broad allowlists can suppress malicious activity.

questions.question: What is a better response to missing audit logs?
options: Document uncertainty and restore logging coverage
questions.why: Lack of telemetry weakens conclusions; restore controls and use remaining independent sources.

questions.question: How should suspected data exfiltration be worded when only DNS is available?
options: Suspicious DNS behavior; data transfer unconfirmed
An attacker was identified by name
questions.why: DNS patterns alone do not prove outbound content disclosure.

questions.question: What is the most important validation before disabling a service account?
options: Business owner, impact and authorized containment plan
questions.why: Service accounts may run critical workloads; coordinated control is needed.

questions.question: A detection stopped after parser field renaming. What should be fixed first?
options: Field mapping, positive fixtures and regression tests
questions.why: Root cause is broken schema contract; repair and validate it.

questions.question: What does ATT&CK rule-count coverage fail to measure?
options: Actual telemetry availability and tested behavior detection
The number of MITRE technique names
questions.why: A rule tag is not evidence of deployed effective detection.

questions.question: A purple-team test misses on one host because Sysmon is not installed. What is gap?
questions.why: Data source gap must be corrected before logic can be judged.

questions.question: What makes a threat-hunt hypothesis testable?
options: Observable behavior, population, timeframe and required data
questions.why: You must define what evidence could support or disconfirm the hypothesis.

questions.question: What is essential for memory acquisition?
options: Legal/operational authorization, impact planning and artifact integrity
questions.why: Volatile collection has risk and privacy considerations.

questions.question: Which metric may falsely improve during connector outages?
questions.why: Missing records can make dashboards seem quiet.

questions.question: How should a detection-as-code rollout be done?
options: Reviewed tests, staging/canary, telemetry monitoring and rollback
Only optimizing for zero false positives
questions.why: Rules need QA, operational performance checks and version control.

questions.question: Why are Kubernetes secret-read events contextual?
options: Controllers may legitimately read secrets, so compare identity/role/change
Every secret get is attacker activity
questions.why: Evaluate service account, namespace, verb and baseline.

questions.question: What is the purpose of purple teaming?
options: Validate attack-path visibility and detections through coordinated safe exercises
Attribute every alert to an APT
questions.why: A structured exercise reveals measurement gaps and detection improvements.

queries.title: Failed logons by user & source
queries.code:
index=windows EventCode=4625 earliest=-24h
| stats count as failures by user, src_ip
| sort - failures
queries.meaning: Investigate repeated failed authentication attempts; field names depend on the parser.

queries.title: New service installation
queries.code:
index=windows EventCode=7045 earliest=-7d
| table _time host ServiceName ImagePath AccountName
queries.meaning: Review new services and unusual image paths on critical endpoints.

queries.title: Suspicious child processes
queries.code:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*\WINWORD.EXE" OR ParentImage="*\EXCEL.EXE")
| table _time host Image ParentImage CommandLine
queries.meaning: Find Office processes launching child programs; tune with known legitimate workflows.

queries.title: Cloud sign-in failures
queries.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| summarize Failures=countif(ResultType != "0"), Successes=countif(ResultType == "0") by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress
| where Failures >= 5
| order by Failures desc
queries.meaning: Find identity-source clusters, then review successful access, devices and MFA.

queries.title: Rare remote logons
queries.code:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4624 and LogonType == 10
| summarize Hosts=dcount(Computer), Events=count() by Account
| order by Hosts desc
queries.meaning: Demonstrates a pivot for remote interactive sessions; check schema and baseline.

queries.title: Cloud management privilege change
queries.code:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue has_any ("roleAssignments/write", "policyAssignments/write")
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, OperationNameValue, ActivityStatusValue, ResourceGroup
queries.meaning: Look for cloud role/policy changes; actual provider fields and operation IDs vary.

queries.title: One host scanning many ports
queries.code:
index=firewall action=allowed earliest=-2h
| stats dc(dest_port) as ports dc(dest_ip) as hosts by src_ip
| where ports > 20 OR hosts > 30
| sort - ports
queries.meaning: Hypothesis for unusual destination diversity, requiring asset-role baselines.

queries.title: Domain frequency & unusual labels
queries.code:
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| summarize Requests=count(), Names=dcount(Name) by ClientIP, QueryType
| order by Requests desc
queries.meaning: Illustrative custom DNS schema: adapt table and field names in your environment.

queries.title: Remote service installs by host
queries.code:
index=windows sourcetype=WinEventLog:System EventCode=7045 earliest=-7d
| stats count values(ServiceName) as services by host
| sort -count
queries.meaning: Validate service creation events and privileged change windows; parser field names vary.

queries.title: Rare interactive logons
queries.code:
index=windows EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10 earliest=-7d
| stats dc(src_ip) as sources count by Account_Name host
| sort -sources
queries.meaning: Use remote interactive logons to find rare origins, then correlate with authorized jump servers.

queries.title: Top blocked WAF clients
queries.code:
index=waf action=block earliest=-24h
| stats count dc(uri_path) as distinct_paths by src_ip
| sort -count
queries.meaning: Volume indicates attempted activity, not successful application exploitation.

queries.title: Process launch after office app
queries.code:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 ParentImage="*\winword.exe"
| table _time host User Image CommandLine ParentImage
| sort -_time
queries.meaning: Hunt suspicious children of Office; compare signed installers and legitimate automation.

queries.title: Identify telemetry freshness
queries.code:
index=edr earliest=-6h
| stats latest(_time) as last_event by host
| eval minutes_lag=(now()-last_event)/60
| sort -minutes_lag
queries.meaning: Do not claim a host is clean when its sensor events are stale.

queries.title: Windows interactive sessions
queries.code:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4624 and LogonType == 10
| summarize Sessions=count() by Computer, Account, IpAddress
| order by Sessions desc
queries.meaning: Requires corresponding fields and successful ingestion of SecurityEvent.

queries.title: Windows process suspicious parent
queries.code:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe", "excel.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "wscript.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
queries.meaning: Microsoft Defender advanced hunting schema may differ from Sentinel tables.

queries.title: Audit unfamiliar mailbox rules
queries.code:
OfficeActivity
| where Operation in ("New-InboxRule", "Set-InboxRule")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, OfficeObjectId, Parameters, ClientIP
queries.meaning: Investigate external forwarding with user sign-ins and mailbox audit events.

queries.title: Entra sign-in failure pivots
queries.code:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResultType != "0"
| summarize Failed=count(), Accounts=dcount(UserPrincipalName) by IPAddress
| order by Accounts desc
queries.meaning: Differentiate spraying behavior from one mistyped password.

queries.title: Audit rare cloud privileges
queries.code:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue has_any ("roleAssignments/write", "authorization")
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, OperationNameValue, ActivityStatusValue
queries.meaning: Add business context and confirm actual provider operation names in your workspace.

queries.title: DNS TXT query frequency
queries.code:
DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) and QueryType == "TXT"
| summarize QueryCount=count(), Domains=dcount(Name) by ClientIP
| order by QueryCount desc
queries.meaning: DnsEvents is illustrative; adapt to actual DNS table and field names.

queries.title: Group lateral authentication origins
queries.code:
index=windows EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=3 earliest=-24h
| stats dc(host) as distinct_targets count by src_ip user
| sort -distinct_targets
queries.meaning: Normalize account and source fields before deciding whether remote auth spreads across machines.

queries.title: Service creation coverage test
queries.code:
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d) and EventLog == "System" and EventID == 7045
| summarize Hosts=dcount(Computer), Events=count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
queries.meaning: Confirm your connector maps System service-install events before deploying this rule.

drills.title: Find the spray origin
drills.task: Return every event in the login-spray case (s01), but nothing from other cases.
drills.hint: Group by case ID before you pivot.
drills.lesson: A targeted case slice defines the scope before behavior inspection.

drills.title: Failed password attempts
drills.task: Find only the failed IdP sign-ins from case s01.
drills.hint: Use AND to narrow the case to results that contain FAIL.
drills.lesson: A failure count alone is insufficient: correlate the eventual success separately.

drills.title: Suspicious successful login
drills.task: Isolate the successful authentication in case s01, excluding token issuance.
drills.hint: SUCCESS and TOKEN_ISSUED are distinct observed events.
drills.lesson: The success after spray can signal compromise; check session actions.

drills.title: Endpoint script chain
drills.task: Return all Sysmon records for the Office macro case s03.
drills.hint: Sysmon is the source; EDR is a separate record.
drills.lesson: Sysmon 1/3/11 support process, connection and file pivots.

drills.title: DNS TXT pattern
drills.task: Find DNS events in case s04.
drills.hint: Narrow by case and log source.
drills.lesson: Only the DNS records belong in this analytic sample; EDR is a follow-up.

drills.title: Approved scanner network events
drills.task: Return firewall records from scanner case s05, excluding change ticket.
drills.lesson: Change tickets are enrichment, not firewall traffic.

drills.title: WAF activity
drills.task: Find the WAF records in case s07, not the app result.
drills.hint: WAF and app are distinct sources.
drills.lesson: WAF block events cannot on their own prove app compromise.

drills.title: Service install event
drills.task: Find System-channel service creation in case s08.
drills.hint: EventID=7045 appears in the service install record.
drills.lesson: Pair service creation with logon origin and process context.

drills.title: Mail audit after phish
drills.task: Return Microsoft 365 audit events from case s09.
drills.hint: Use source=audit for mailbox rule and access records.
drills.lesson: Rules and MailItemsAccessed create the post-login activity chain.

drills.title: Ransomware EDR actions
drills.task: Return all EDR events from ransomware case s10.
drills.hint: Filter by case and EDR, not all file-server telemetry.
drills.lesson: EDR process behavior must be interpreted with file system impact.

drills.title: Remote service creation trail
drills.task: Return System-channel events from case s11.
drills.hint: System events contain two service installations.
drills.lesson: The same service name on two hosts supports lateral movement hypotheses.

drills.title: AWS audit trail
drills.task: Return CloudTrail events from case s12.
drills.hint: Only cloudtrail events, not change audit.
drills.lesson: Management and object access events form a privilege/data timeline.

drills.title: Beacon proxy callbacks
drills.task: Return proxy traffic in case s13.
drills.hint: Proxy traffic excludes Sysmon binary provenance.

drills.title: Detection engineering metrics
drills.task: Return metric events from case s14.
drills.lesson: Precision cannot be optimized by removing telemetry.

drills.title: Missing sensor facts
drills.task: Find health events from case s15.
drills.hint: Separate health from SIEM query count.
drills.lesson: Zero hits from a disconnected source is not a healthy SOC.

drills.title: Post-incident review evidence
drills.task: Return post-incident review records in case s16.
drills.hint: Every synthetic record here is from review source.
drills.lesson: An evidence-led PIR produces owned improvements.

drills.title: Malicious OAuth grant chain
drills.task: Return audit events from suspicious consent case s23.
drills.hint: Identify the app consent and application secret operations.

drills.title: Linux suspicious execution
drills.task: Return auditd exec events in Linux persistence case s25.
drills.hint: Linux auditd records capture process invocation.
drills.lesson: Systemd file writes and SSH provide supporting events.

drills.title: Rule regression fixture
drills.task: Return synthetic test-fixture events from parser regression case s28.
drills.hint: Select test fixtures, not all pipeline events.
drills.lesson: A passing test requires parsed fields matching rule assumptions.
